newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH AGENCY LOWERS GRAIN QUALITY PURCHASE NORMS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH AGENCY LOWERS GRAIN QUALITY PURCHASE NORMS.

text.p: Poland's state food market regulator, the Agriculture Market Agency (ARR) said in a Tuesday statement it decided to lower some of the quality requirements for grain purchased from farmers.

"The decision has been made in line with expectations of farmers, who need to sell the grain they have produced. It will still be bread-quality grain," the ARR's spokesman Stanislaw Myslinski told Reuters.
"The grain the farmers offer is just marginally below the standard parameters," he added.
The statement said the ARR lowered the parameter of gluten solubility and Hagberg falling time and left gluten content, contamination level and grain equalization unchanged.
The Agency said it has so far bought 9,300 tonnes of wheat and 6,500 tonnes of rye to replenish its reserves from the planned 190,000 tonnes and 65,000 tonnes respectively.

ARR authorised private warehouses have so far bought 2,831 tonnes of wheat and 4,800 tonnes of rye from a planned overall total of 1.75 million tonnes. The authorised warehouses use preferential credit to buy the grain but have to use ARR set prices.
The agency is paying 530 zlotys per tonne of wheat and 370 zlotys per tonne of rye.
